candidates.title: [3.14] gh-159864: Fix syslog.openlog() crash with concurrent sys.argv changes (GH-159884)
candidates.body:
syslog_get_argv() took sys.argv[0] with PyList_GetItem() and increfed it only afterwards, so on the free-threaded build a concurrent replacement of sys.argv[0] could free it in between. Use PyList_GetItemRef() instead. (cherry picked from commit e5e0748abd27e39655cb8dc313a82cad6563c54f)

candidates.title: gh-159684: Modernize string formatting and simplify constructs in configparser
candidates.body:
Brings `Lib/configparser.py` and `Lib/test/test_configparser.py` up to Ruff's
default rule set, which reported 72 findings across the two files. CPython's
own Ruff configuration only selects `F401` and `F811` for `Lib/`, so nothing
here was failing; the motivation is readability plus keeping the module
convergent with its PyPI backport, which lints with the defaults and would
otherwise need a per-file exemption for exactly these two files
(jaraco/configparser#73).

Four commits, each reviewable on its own:

1. **f-strings** (`UP030`, `UP031`, `UP032`) — the autofixable conversions,
   with the lines that would have exceeded 79 columns rewrapped by hand. The
   rendered strings are unchanged; `%%` escapes collapse to `%` as the `%`
   operator did.
2. **Simplifications** — `C405`, `C408`, `C414`, `RUF019`, `RUF059`, `F841`,
   `SIM102`, `SIM117`, and parenthesizing an implicit string concatenation
   inside a list literal (`ISC004`) so it does not read as a missing comma.
3. **The remaining `%` sites** that Ruff declines to autofix because the `%d`
   conversions are not provably integral. Converted by hand, keeping an
   explicit `:d` so a non-integer still raises rather than being coerced.
4. **Imports, `__all__`, and `ClassVar`** (`I001`, `RUF022`, `RUF012`).

The last one is the only part with a design decision in it. `RUF012` wants
`BOOLEAN_STATES` annotated `ClassVar`, and the obvious spelling would import
`typing` at runtime — which this module deliberately avoids, per the
`gh-117703` note above its imports. So it adds `from __future__ import
annotations` and imports `ClassVar` only under `TYPE_CHECKING`, the same shape
`Lib/tomllib/_parser.py` and `Lib/importlib/metadata/__init__.py` use (both
also kept in sync with a PyPI backport). `python -X importtime -c "import
configparser"` confirms `typing` stays out of the import graph. Deferring
annotations also lets `Iterable['ParsingError']` drop its quotes (`UP037`).

That does make `TYPE_CHECKING` a module-level name, so it joins `Error` in
`not_exported` in the `check__all__` test.

`C901` on `ExtendedInterpolation._interpolate_some` (13 > 10) is the one
finding not fixed. It is a measurement, not a defect, and no small edit
satisfies it, so it gets `# noqa: C901  # gh-159686`; gh-159686 records why the
branching is inherent to the interpolation grammar and sketches a possible
refactoring, so the suppression is documented rather than silent.

With all four applied, both CPython's Ruff configuration and the default rule
set report no findings for either file, at `py310` and `py314` targets.
`test_configparser`, `test_logging`, `test_collections`, `test___all__` and
`test_pydoc` pass.

NEWS entry added under `Library`; there is no user-visible behavior change.

* Issue: gh-159684
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

auto_merge.commit_message:
* gh-159684: Use f-strings in configparser and its tests

Convert the remaining printf-style and str.format() call sites in
Lib/configparser.py and Lib/test/test_configparser.py to f-strings
(Ruff UP030, UP031, UP032), rewrapping the lines that would otherwise
exceed 79 columns. No behavior change; the rendered strings are
identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gh-159684: Simplify a few constructs in configparser and its tests

Apply the straightforward simplifications Ruff reports for these two
modules: redundant list() calls (C408, C414), a literal set (C405),
a key check that get() already covers (RUF019), an unpacked value that
is never used (RUF059), an unused assertRaises binding (F841),
collapsible if statements (SIM102) and nested with statements (SIM117).
Also parenthesize an implicit string concatenation inside a list
literal (ISC004) so it is not mistaken for a missing comma.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gh-159684: Convert the last percent-formatting in configparser

Ruff leaves these UP031 sites alone because the %d conversions are not
provably integral, so convert them by hand, keeping the explicit :d
format spec so a non-integer still raises rather than being coerced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gh-159684: Clear the remaining Ruff findings in configparser

Sort the imports (I001) and __all__ (RUF022), and annotate the mutable
class attributes as ClassVar (RUF012). The ClassVar annotation would
otherwise mean importing typing at runtime, which this module avoids,
so defer annotations with __future__ instead and import ClassVar only
under TYPE_CHECKING, as tomllib and importlib.metadata do. Deferring
annotations also lets ParsingError be referenced unquoted (UP037).

ExtendedInterpolation._interpolate_some gets an explicit noqa: C901,
tagged with gh-159686, which records why the complexity is inherent to
the interpolation grammar and what a refactoring might look like.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gh-159684: Add a NEWS entry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
